title: Microfield runbook — tiny experiment tracker
content:
Purpose: small personal tracker for quick microbench variants — capture a few runs, notes-to-self, and immediate hypotheses. Meant for noisy, fast iter; not canonical lab sheet.

Context:
- Running local / dev cluster experiments to validate int8 vs fp16 effect on p95 latency and token throughput for conversational model family 'osmosis-v1'.
- Using Redwood dev account (temp key), sampling 128-token prompts, single-request steady-state cache warmed.

Quick measurement protocol (notes-to-self):
1) Start node with --max-batch=8, --prefill-cache true.
2) Send 50 sequential single-user requests (no concurrency) to warm KV cache, then 200 requests with concurrency set to 4.
3) Report p50/p90/p95, tokens/sec measured server-side and client-side RTT.
4) Estimate cost_per_1k_tokens using cheap-metrics: (gpu-minutes * hourly-cost)/tokens_generated * 1000.

Table: concise run log (most recent at top)

trial_id,variant,quant,batch_size,seq_len,concurrency,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_s,cost_per_1k,notes
T-2026-03-09a,osmosis-v1,fp16,8,128,4,45,120,320,0.28,baseline fp16
T-2026-03-09b,osmosis-v1,int8,8,128,4,42,135,360,0.19,better throughput but slightly higher p95 — investigate attention kernel
T-2026-02-25a,osmosis-v1,int8-qat,4,64,2,38,98,410,0.22,small batch QAT run; surprisingly low p95
T-2025-12-10c,osmosis-lite,int8,8,128,4,33,80,500,0.12,cheap tiny model baseline for cost comps

Immediate observations:
- int8 (naive quant) tends to push tokens/sec up (10–30%) for these seq lengths, but depending on kernel selection p95 can sometimes regresses (~5–15ms). Need to capture variance (stdev) next time.
- Smaller batch_size (4 vs 8) gave lower p95 in one run (likely reduced queuing); note trade-off vs throughput.
- QAT variant is promising; schedule follow-up to run 3 seeds.

Open actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run T-2026-03-09b with nvprof traced kernel selection (log kernels) — link to GH PR above.
- [ ] Add stdev and 99th percentile to table.
- [ ] Script cost calc (tiny python snippet) and save in experiments/mini-costs.ipynb.
- [ ] Compare with dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-1) to check infra variance (ticket JIRA-9876).

Short heuristics for next runs:
- Always warm-cache with 50 sequential requests.
- Run 3 seeds (different random prompts) for stable numbers when comparing major configs.
- Capture per-request token count and server-side token emit timestamps in logs.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- If p95 spikes only on int8, check for slow memcpy or suboptimal kernel fallback on sequence length 128. Might be windowed attention fallback.
- Try pinned memory path and measure host<->device copy times separately.

Scratch calculations (example):
- observed tokens_total = 200 req * 128 tokens = 25,600 tokens; run_time = 80s => tokens/s = 320 => cost_per_1k = (gpu_hours * hourly_cost)/tokens * 1000. If gpu-hours=0.0022 and hourly_cost=$3 => cost_per_1k = (0.0022*3)/25600*1000 ≈ $0.00026 (sanity check — inconsistent with table numbers, refine with real pricing).

End of page — short-term log only. Keep this file for quick scribbles; move cleaned tables to shared experiments folder once stable.
